name: Calcium Deficiency
description: Calcium is essential for cell wall structure and root development. Deficiency causes distorted new growth, blossom end rot in fruits, and poor root systems. It is common in acidic, leached tropical soils.
symptoms: Blossom end rot in tomato and pepper fruits (dark sunken area at fruit tip)
Death of growing points and terminal buds
Young leaves showing distortion, crinkling, and chlorosis
Poor root development with short, stubby roots
Fruit cracking and reduced storage quality
causes: Acidic soils (pH <5.5) with low calcium availability
Irregular watering causing calcium transport issues
High nitrogen or potassium levels competing with calcium uptake
Saline or sodic soils reducing calcium absorption
treatments: Apply agricultural lime (calcium carbonate) or gypsum (calcium sulfate)
Foliar spray of calcium chloride (0.5-1%) or calcium nitrate
Use calcium nitrate as a soluble calcium source
Maintain consistent soil moisture for calcium transport
prevention: Conduct soil testing and lime to raise pH to 6.0-6.5
Use dolomitic lime to supply both calcium and magnesium
Irrigate regularly and evenly to maintain consistent moisture
Avoid excessive nitrogen and potassium fertilization
